brief.subject: IRS finalizes rules on paying taxes by card
brief.headline: IRS Finalizes Card-Payment Rules Under the Taxpayer First Act
brief.dek: Final IRS rules on card tax payments, MFA expectations for firms, a Tax Court easement ruling, and a partial withdrawal of spinoff rules.
brief.lede: The IRS has issued final regulations that reflect a law change allowing it to take credit and debit card tax payments directly, without routing taxpayers to outside processors.

sections.heading: IRS Card Payments Get Final Rules
bullets: Final IRS regulations on paying tax by commercially acceptable means were published October 19.
They reflect Taxpayer First Act changes allowing the IRS to accept credit or debit card payments directly.
That could cut out third-party payment processors when you pay federal tax by card.
The rules also lift restrictions on the IRS paying fees under card-payment contracts.

sections.heading: MFA Is Expected, Not Optional
bullets: The FTC Safeguards Rule and the IRS expect multifactor authentication on every system holding client data.
Tax and accounting firms that disable MFA over user fatigue risk falling short of that expectation.
Attackers are designing schemes specifically to get around MFA prompts, so staff training matters too.

sections.heading: Tax Court Rejects Easement Deductions
bullets: The Tax Court disallowed deductions tied to historic structure conservation easements.
Owners weighing easement write-offs on historic buildings should expect close scrutiny of their claims.

sections.heading: Spinoff Rule Proposal Partly Pulled
bullets: The IRS partially withdrew proposed Section 355 regulations on the device prohibition and active trade or business test.
Those rules govern tax-free distributions of a controlled corporation's stock.
Closely held corporations planning a split-up should check which proposed provisions remain in play.

items.title: Proposed Rule: Guidance Under Section 355 Concerning Device and Active Trade or Business; Partial Withdrawal
items.snippet: This document partially withdraws a notice of proposed rulemaking containing proposed regulations regarding the application of the device prohibition and the active trade or business requirement for distributions of controlled corporation stock (or stock and securities) by a distributing corporation without income, gain, or loss. The proposed regulations would affect corporations and their shareholders and security holders.

items.title: Rule: Regulations Regarding Payment of Tax by Commercially Acceptable Means
items.snippet: This document contains final regulations regarding the payment of tax by commercially acceptable means. The final regulations reflect changes to the law made by the Taxpayer First Act that would allow the IRS to directly accept payments of tax by credit or debit card, without having to connect taxpayers to third-party payment processors. These final regulations remove restrictions on the payment of any fee by the IRS under any contracts related to payment of taxes by credit, debit, or charge car
